subsystems.name: Bioink and cell supply
subsystems.role: provides the living material that will become the organ tissue.
parts: human cells (induced pluripotent stem cells or primary cells)

subsystems.name: Bioprinting hardware
subsystems.role: deposits bioink and cells with micrometre precision.

subsystems.name: Microfluidic chip
subsystems.role: houses the printed tissue and supplies nutrients while removing waste.

subsystems.name: Vascular network
subsystems.role: mimics blood vessels to keep thick tissue alive.
parts: sacrificial inks that are later dissolved

subsystems.name: Sensing and readout
subsystems.role: measures how the tissue responds to drugs or disease.

buildSteps.title: Design the tissue architecture
buildSteps.detail: Computer models define where each cell type and material will go, often based on medical imaging of real organs.

buildSteps.title: Prepare bioink and cells
buildSteps.detail: Cells are expanded in culture, mixed with hydrogel precursors, and loaded into sterile cartridges.

buildSteps.title: Print the construct
buildSteps.detail: The bioprinter layers bioink and support material to build a 3D tissue, typically a few millimetres thick.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the chip
buildSteps.detail: The printed tissue is placed in the microfluidic chip, and fluidic connections are sealed.

buildSteps.title: Vascularize and mature
buildSteps.detail: Endothelial cells are seeded into channels; over days to weeks, the tissue matures and forms functional units.

buildSteps.title: Perfuse and maintain
buildSteps.detail: A pump circulates nutrient medium at body temperature (37 °C) to keep the tissue alive.

buildSteps.title: Test and analyse
buildSteps.detail: Drugs are introduced through the chip, and sensors or microscopy record the tissue's response.

prerequisites.why: provides a renewable source of human cells for printing.
enables precise control of fluids at the microscale.
simple tissues can be printed, but complex organs with blood vessels remain difficult.
without blood vessels, printed tissue thicker than a few hundred micrometres dies from lack of oxygen.
regulators need proof that these models predict drug effects better than animals.

pathway.milestone: single-organ chips (liver, kidney, heart) used in drug discovery
pathway.unlocks: earlier detection of drug toxicity, reducing animal testing.

pathway.milestone: bioprinted multi-organ chips with vascular networks
pathway.unlocks: more realistic models for testing drug metabolism and side effects.

pathway.milestone: patient-derived cells integrated into printed chips
pathway.unlocks: personalized drug testing to find the best treatment for an individual.
regulatory acceptance as replacements for animal testing and better prediction of human responses.
